messages:
Amy Chen: Quick — Pinegrove retail POC final readout. Deck review tomorrow 10:00 PT. I pasted the final numbers below, need sign-off on success criteria + clear next-step asks. cc @Raj Patel @Leo Martin :eyes:

Amy Chen: Final metrics (aggregated across 3 stores, 2 weeks):
```
Throughput (avg reqs/s): 120
Latency p50: 38ms, p95: 110ms
Tokens per session (avg): 420
Embedding recall @k=5: 0.82
Top-1 accuracy (intent classification): 0.91
Cost (hosted) per 1k tokens: $0.80
Estimated monthly cost at scale (100k sessions/mo): ~$8.4k
```

Amy Chen: Success criteria we agreed: latency p95 < 150ms, intent acc >= 0.9, embedding recall >= 0.8, and ops runbook for fallbacks. We passed latency and accuracy, recall is slightly above threshold but has edge cases.

Raj Patel: Congrats team. Security Qs for the readout: Pinegrove wants the data flow diagram + confirmation of encryption at rest + KMS integration notes. Also need an answer on SOC2 timeline if they push for it in contracting.

Leo Martin: Nice numbers. On pricing/scale: they asked for a committed capacity quote for 6 months. I ran a quick reserve calc — if they commit to 200k sessions/mo we can offer 18% discount with Dedicated capacity. Need engineering confirmation on achievable autoscale burst.

Maria Gomez: On quality: we ran 120 prompt variations. Problems concentrated on humor-heavy copy where embeddings drift. Attached the eval snippets in the deck. For readout, recommend showing 3 prompt examples: one success, one partial fail, one fail + remediation plan. Also propose a mini A/B result: prompt tuning reduced hallucination rate by ~30%.

Chris O'Neill: Ops notes: KV cache warmup policy helped p50 but p95 still spikes on certain long-tail product detail queries. We have two mitigations: 1) prefix caching for frequent SKUs, 2) a small model fallback route (faster quantized variant). Both are in our runbook. For Dedicated, autoscale can do a 2x burst for 10min windows; for longer bursts we'd need headroom.

Amy Chen: Awesome. For the readout deck — slide owners?

Leo Martin: I'll take pricing/scale slide and the proposed Dedicated config.

Raj Patel: I'll own security/compliance slide and attach the data flow diagram. I need the exact KMS config from Chris — can you paste the snippet?

Chris O'Neill: Sure. KMS config we used (example):
```yaml
kms:
  provider: aws-kms
  key_id: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
  encrypt_in_transit: true
  encrypt_at_rest: true
```
Feel free to redact account ids for the deck.

Maria Gomez: I'll own the evals slide + prompt examples. Note: show the exact prompt, expected answer, and score. Keep it short.

Amy Chen: I'll stitch the slides and run a dry-run at 9:00 PT tomorrow. Action items: Leo (pricing) due EOD, Raj (security diagram + SOC2 timeline note) due EOD, Maria (eval slide + prompts) due EOD, Chris (KMS snippet + ops runbook summary) due EOD.

Leo Martin: ack. I'll also include the committed-capacity pricing table and an optional pay-as-you-go fallback.

Raj Patel: ack. I'll add a note: SOC2 readiness is in progress, expected audit availability Q3 — caveat in the slide.

Chris O'Neill: ack. I'll paste runbook bullets and the fallback routing policy.

deploy-bot: Deployed infra-change 202-redis-prefixing to staging at 2023-06-11T18:42:10Z :white_check_mark:

Amy Chen: One more big question for the readout: expansion ask. We should propose a 3-phase path: pilot -> region-rollout -> enterprise SLA (Dedicated + annual commit). Leo, can you sketch estimated unit economics for each phase?

Leo Martin: Yes — I'll include a slide: pilot (hosted) unit cost = $0.008/token effective, region-rollout (hybrid) = $0.006/token, Dedicated SLA = $0.0045/token with 12mo commit. Will add sensitivity scenarios.

Maria Gomez: Also recommend recommending a 4-week eval window post-readout to validate prompt fixes with A/B.

Amy Chen: Great. If no other blockers, I'll assemble and send the deck link here by 8:30 PT for the 9:00 dry-run. Thanks everyone :v:
